h: לְעֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, ד׳ Erev Yom Kippur, 4

p: "Whoever eats and drinks on the ninth,
as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth."
And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained
(רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ט, א, ד״ה כָּל הָאוֹכֵל):
"And since his eating counts as an affliction,
the more one increases in eating and drinking,
And elsewhere Rashi, of blessed memory, explained
so that you will be able to fast on the tenth."
it would have been enough for him to eat ordinary foods,
as long as he is satisfied,
such as bread and the like,
and not necessarily costly and fine foods.
Yet we find in the Gemara
שֶׁהָיוּ מְהַדְּרִים אַחַר בָּשָׂר וְדָגִים דַּיְיקָא,
that they would seek out specifically meat and fish,
as is stated in the Mishnah (Chullin 83a):
and according to Rabbi Yose HaGelili,
"also on Erev Yom Kippur in the Galil" —
for there they would seek out the meat of cattle,
while in Yehudah and other places
they would seek out the meat of fowl,
in the first perek of Kesubos
And as we find in the Midrash
in the story of the tailor
what the special importance of this day is,
that one should eat fine foods on it.
as is stated in the writings of the Arizal,
there is the utterance of Hashem's mouth
וּבַחַי יֵשׁ יוֹתֵר מוֹצָא פִּי ה׳
and in a living creature there is more of the utterance of Hashem's mouth
for wheat amounts in gematria to twenty-two,
corresponding to the twenty-two letters of the Torah.
Therefore it is a food of importance for man,
And when the animal eats it,
it then rises to a higher level
through being eaten by the animal.
"I — neither in my poverty did I eat vegetables,
in the place where vegetables would go in,
let meat and fish go in."
This too is to be explained:
when he was on a lower level,
to eat food from a living thing,
he was able to rectify all the more
the foods that have more vitality in them.
"As long as I have not eaten ox meat,
גַּם כֵּן שֶׁהָיָה רְצוֹנוֹ יוֹתֵר בְּבָשָׂר
this too means that his desire was more for meat
because of the greater holiness that a living creature has.
that one eats on the ninth
for the fast of the tenth day,
this is the honor due to the tenth day:
that he eats on the ninth,
which have more holy vitality in them.
since it is a mitzvah to eat on the ninth,
And according to what I have written,
for here the mitzvah is not to indulge oneself,
For behold, it is stated in the holy Zohar
"Whoever eats and drinks on the ninth
with the affliction of the soul in two portions."
And in the glosses on the holy Zohar
"Since the affliction comes out of pleasure,
and so it is like two afflictions.
the fast is an affliction of the body
and the eating is an affliction of the soul."
וּפֵירוּשׁ זֶה הוּא גַּם כֵּן בַּשְּׁלָ״ה
And this explanation is also in the Shelah
But he rejected this second explanation,
for it is written, "for having sinned against the soul"
this refers to one who sits in a fast;
and it seems that the first explanation is the main one.
But in truth, this too does not seem right.
Besides the fact that the matter itself,
as it plainly appears, is that
it is easier to fast the next day,
so that what he wrote does not seem right,
that through this there will be
a greater affliction the next day —
the reason for the eating and drinking
is so that one will be able to fast,
And also, in the Midrash cited above
it says that it is in honor of Yom Kippur,
whereas according to his view it is the reverse;
וּמַה יְּקָרָא דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים יֵשׁ בָּזֶה
for what honor to Yom Kippur is there in this,
that one should feel more affliction?
for it explains "two portions" as body and soul.
And in truth this is said afterwards
that it refers to what is said, "your souls,"
in the plural, regarding the soul,
since it does not say "your soul";
is that it is His will, may His Name be blessed,
to forgive us all our sins;
the root of the beginning of Adam HaRishon's sin,
which began with a matter of eating.
And they said in the Midrash
מִי יְגַלֶּה עָפָר מֵעֵינֶיךָ, אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן,
"Who will remove the dust from your eyes, Adam HaRishon!
You could not withstand your command
and behold, your children wait out orlah
And this is the rectification of his sin.
is not yet complete for all of Yisrael,
for it applies only to those
who have in their vineyard or garden
no other trees of this species,
and also find none to buy,
or have nothing with which to buy
that has already passed out of orlah,
so that he has nothing of that species to eat,
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן מַמְתִּין שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים.
and nevertheless he waits three years.
אָמְנָם מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עוֹד מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין,
But one who has more of that species —
זֶה לֹא יוּכַל לְתַקֵּן עוֹד יִצְרוֹ בְּכָךְ,
he cannot further rectify his inclination by this,
for what great feat is it that he waits,
since he has some of that species?
we were commanded to fast completely,
and not merely for one hour
but for a full twenty-four hours.
the sin of Adam HaRishon in full,
and the aspect of is'hapcha, transformation.
that one transforms everything into holiness.
And the rectification of Adam HaRishon's eating
he does not eat for the body's pleasure,
because it was good and desirable
but only for the sake of holiness,
"A tzaddik eats to satisfy his soul" —
is only to sustain his soul.
As we find with Rabbeinu HaKadosh,
who would eat all the delicacies in the world,
for his table was a table of kings
(בְּרָכוֹת נז, ב; עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יא, א),
"I did not benefit even with my little finger"
And with Hillel HaZaken, who said
that he was going to do kindness
עִם אַכְסַנְיָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
with a guest he had in his house,
and he was referring to himself
The affliction and the fast on Yom Kippur
and the body is afflicted by this,
in that it does not eat or drink at all.
And likewise there is an affliction of the soul
namely, that he compels his soul and his heart,
so that although he eats delicacies,
it should be without any bodily pleasure,
only because it is a mitzvah to eat on the ninth
and because Hashem Yisbarach commanded it.
to fast on the ninth as well,
with an unbroken fast of two days,
And likewise, when He commanded us to eat and delight,
אָנוּ אוֹכְלִים רַק בִּשְׁבִיל מִצְוַת הַשֵּׁם לְבַד
we eat only for the sake of Hashem's mitzvah alone,
and not to give the body pleasure at all.
And this is the intent of the holy Zohar
"And he is found on the tenth
with the affliction of the soul in two portions":
that is, from the side of the fast,
which is the affliction of the body,
and affliction of the soul from the side of is'hapcha,
for the strength for the fast on the tenth
that he eats on the ninth
without any pleasure of his own.
And the need to purify the soul
is alluded to in that it is written "your souls,"
כִּי מִשְׁכַּן הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הוּא בַּלֵּב,
For the dwelling place of the yetzer hara is in the heart,
and the heart has two chambers:
"The heart of a wise man is at his right,
and the heart of a fool at his left" (Koheles 10:2).
that the yetzer hara resembles a fly
which sits upon the two openings of the heart;
and it wishes to make even the wise heart sin,
"For there is no righteous man on earth
who does good and does not sin" —
that is, in the good deed itself,
from the side of the wise heart,
to bring some flaw into its performance,
so that he not do it
according to His will, may His Name be blessed.
And these are the two souls within man:
the soul in the wise heart
and the soul in the foolish heart.
serve to nullify the power of the inclination
in both chambers of the heart.
nullify the inclination in the left chamber,
nullifies the power of the inclination
that dwells at the opening of the wise heart,
הֲנָאַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה גַּם כֵּן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
the pleasure of this world into holiness as well.
And with this, the question of Tosafos is answered:
here it does not apply at all to say
for the eating of Erev Yom Kippur
is precisely so that it not be "for you":
no bodily pleasure at all from the eating,
only from the side of holiness, since it is a mitzvah to eat.
And when it says regarding Yom Tov
and that is the mitzvah performed with the body.
even if he has no intention at all
but only to give his body pleasure,
And in the writings of the Arizal it is stated
that it is all in holiness; see there.
on the contrary, its mitzvah is
that his eating not be intended "for you"
or for his bodily pleasure at all,
but only for Hashem, to fulfill Hashem's mitzvah.
And this is the meaning of
"as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth,"
as if he had been commanded to fast.
what virtue is there in "as if he fasted"?
is that he eats with this intention:
that we, according to our recognition
of the magnitude of our sins and our guilt —
to fast two days without a break,
and only through this would He forgive,
we would do it with great joy, as said above;
הוּא רַק בִּשְׁבִיל מִצְוַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּנַּ״ל:
is only for the sake of the mitzvah of Hashem Yisbarach, as said above.
although it is a greater level
is a matter of the inner dimension
and of the hidden things in a person's heart,
Therefore we were commanded on the ninth
so that we be found pleasing before Him, may His Name be blessed,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִמְחוֹל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לָנוּ
so that through this Hashem Yisbarach will forgive us
However, in order also to shut
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לָהֶם פִּתְחוֹן פֶּה לְקַטְרֵג —
so that they have no opening to accuse —
for the angels do not know
the hidden things in the heart,
therefore the mitzvah on Yom Kippur
so that the accusers see in actual deed
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִתְכַּפֵּר לָנוּ עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ.
and through this our sins will be atoned for.
And further, it is stated in the holy Zohar
that the word "es" is expounded everywhere
This is along the lines of
what is stated in Perek Chelek
who set guards in an orchard,
a lame man and a blind man.
"Let us eat of the fruit," etc.
אַחַר כָּךְ הִרְכִּיב הַחִיגֵּר עַל הַסּוּמָא,
Afterwards he set the lame man upon the blind man,
and in this way judged them.
So too the soul and the body:
כָּל אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: אֲנִי לֹא חָטָאתִי;
each one says, "I did not sin";
so they stand the soul and the body together
So too, for the atonement of sins
affliction of the soul and the body together.
And it is stated in the Gemara (Berachos 17a)
regarding Rav Sheshes, who sat in a fast
"Just as I have sat in a fast
and my fat and my blood have diminished,
may it be Your will that my fat and my blood
be as though I had offered it before You on the altar,
and may You accept it favorably."
alludes to the body and the soul together:
the soul is alluded to by the blood,
and "my fat" alludes to the body,
"You grew fat, you grew thick, you grew gross."
And part of a soul is like the whole soul
therefore it is considered as if the whole person
and the Akeidas Yitzchak is remembered.
